title: The app sometimes forgets (disable) certain features that users have enabled (for example, lightswitch)

judgment.rationale: The report describes a recurring loss of an enabled Light Switch state, and the supplied diagnostic triage found no crash signature. The repository has a dedicated Light Switch settings loader and file watcher, so a settings reload, persistence, or initialization boundary is a plausible code-fix area, but the exact transition that clears the setting is not confirmed.
evidence: The reporter uses PowerToys 0.101.2362 stable on Windows build 26200 with a per-user installation and supplied a PowerToys diagnostic ZIP.
The reporter clarified that the feature disables every few days rather than only immediately after an upgrade.
The existing automated triage comment reports no matching error or crash signatures and characterizes the problem as a possible silent state-persistence or module-initialization issue.
LightSwitchSettings loads persisted schedule and theme-target values, watches the settings file, debounces changes, and reloads state asynchronously.
judgment.recommended_action: Run a focused Light Switch state-transition investigation with a fresh diagnostic archive captured immediately after the next spontaneous disable, then implement and test the confirmed persistence or reload fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: No open or merged fix attempt was found for this issue. A repository change is applicable, but the failing state transition still needs to be distinguished between external settings overwrite, debounced reload, and module initialization.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve Light Switch enablement across spontaneous settings reloads
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: a settings-file rewrite or module reload can replace or reinitialize Light Switch state without preserving the user's enabled configuration; the current loader and asynchronous file-watcher path are the most relevant code boundaries.
plan: Trace the Light Switch enablement and schedule/theme-target values from Settings UI persistence through LightSwitchSettings::LoadSettings and module initialization.
Capture the exact settings-file and lifecycle transition that occurs when the feature disables, then guard reload or initialization so unchanged persisted enablement is not reset.
Add regression coverage for debounced settings reload, restart, and an external settings update while Light Switch is enabled.
verification: Reproduce the issue over the reported multi-day interval or with the identified triggering transition and confirm Light Switch remains enabled.
Run the focused Light Switch settings unit tests and verify that a settings reload preserves the persisted enablement and theme-target values.

confidence.rationale: The recurring symptom, silent diagnostic result, and dedicated asynchronous settings reload path align with a plausible state-reset defect, but no trace yet identifies which transition actually clears the setting.

issue_context.summary: Light Switch intermittently turns itself off in stable 0.101.2362 after running for several days. The report includes a diagnostic archive and the author has clarified that the behavior is not tied to upgrading, but the archive and public discussion do not identify the state transition that disables the feature.
known_information: The affected module is Light Switch.
The reporter expects the feature to remain enabled after enabling it.
The reporter has observed the feature disable itself twice since the last installation, approximately every two or three days.
The issue includes a PowerToys diagnostic ZIP captured on 2026-09-07.
Automated triage found no matching error or crash signatures in its analyzed diagnostic subset.
The issue has Issue-Bug, Needs-Triage, and Product-LightSwitch labels and no assignee.
inferences: The symptom may be caused by silent settings persistence, a settings-file reload, or module initialization rather than an exception-driven crash.
Because the failure is intermittent and not upgrade-triggered, a periodic lifecycle or external settings-write boundary is more likely than a one-time installer migration, but this is unconfirmed.
issue_context.analysis: The public evidence supports investigating the Light Switch settings and reload path instead of treating this as a generic crash report. The code's debounced file watcher and LoadSettings method provide concrete ownership signals, while the absence of a captured trigger means a full implementation design would otherwise risk fixing the wrong transition. A fresh archive immediately after reproduction and a precise trigger classification are the smallest additional evidence that can separate competing hypotheses.
initial_investigation: Reviewed LightSwitchSettings.cpp: it loads schedule, latitude/longitude, time offsets, and changeSystem/changeApps values under a mutex; a debounced file watcher calls LoadSettings asynchronously after settings-file changes.
Reviewed recent Light Switch history, including the July 2026 stable profile ID change and earlier settings/refactor work; no linked fix for this issue was identified.
Searched related Light Switch issues; existing results concern scheduling, theme behavior, profiles, and feature requests rather than this intermittent disable symptom.
Reviewed the complete issue body and five comments, including the maintainer question about upgrade correlation and the reporter's answer that the failure occurs every few days.

information_gaps.information: A fresh PowerToys diagnostic archive captured immediately after Light Switch disables itself, plus the exact local time of the transition.
information_gaps.why_needed: This can correlate the spontaneous disable with a settings-file write, restart, sleep/resume, scheduled mode transition, or module error and distinguish the competing root-cause hypotheses.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Please reproduce the problem and submit a comment containing /bugreport immediately after the feature turns off; include the approximate timestamp and whether the PC resumed from sleep or PowerToys restarted.

information_gaps.information: Whether only Light Switch becomes disabled, or whether other PowerToys modules also lose their enabled state at the same time.
information_gaps.why_needed: A single-module symptom points to Light Switch persistence or initialization, while multiple modules would implicate shared settings storage or an installer/update process.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: After the next occurrence, record the enabled/disabled state of the other PowerToys modules before changing any settings.

actions.label: Request Light Switch activation trace
actions.note: Ask for only the evidence needed to identify the intermittent state transition.

comment.body:
Thanks for confirming that Light Switch turns off every few days rather than only after an upgrade, and for providing the first diagnostic report. The current report does not show what event clears the setting. Please provide the next occurrence as follows:

1. Immediately after Light Switch turns off, submit a comment containing /bugreport and include the approximate time it happened; please also note whether the PC had resumed from sleep or PowerToys had restarted.
2. Confirm whether any other PowerToys modules lost their enabled state at the same time.

This will let us distinguish a Light Switch settings reload from a shared settings or lifecycle problem.

actions.label: Design Light Switch state persistence fix
actions.note: Approve a fork-side investigation and implementation focused on the settings reload and initialization boundaries after the targeted evidence is available.
